Confirmed (turn4 design study): export boundary = full 150km-sphere surface (2.8e11 m²); baseline export ceiling 2.8e21 W (liquid-metal coolant, ~10% pipe-exit area × 1e11 W/m²); maxed ceiling ~3e22 W with a dedicated coolant-throughput research line (two-phase/supercritical, extreme velocity, ~1e12 W/m²). BOTH below pure Landauer@300K (2.9e-21 J) — ordinary tiering bottoms at ~100x-Landauer (~2.9e-19 J) and CANNOT reach this; only reversible-credit tiers (below the conventional floor) can. Credit accrues ~1 per 1% compute_fraction/turn at 8% (confirmed 3x: 13→21→29). Turn5: testing 15% fraction to see if it scales linearly past the tier-cap that applies to discretely-tiered params, or is itself capped — watch result next ruling.

## Operation-count reduction (turn4 answer, now SETTLED — stop researching this line)
Rigorous r-RESPA multi-timestep integration (fast bond modes on longer steps, all atoms explicit) accepted: ≤10x reduction, moves rubric floor from 1e43 to 1e42 ops/s sustained in-core. Mean-field/implicit solvent, spatial coarsening, importance sampling REJECTED (violate "every atom, femtosecond steps"). Turn5: redirected that budget into a verification-plan design study (2%) — need a stated, concrete method to prove the core really runs full-fidelity r-RESPA MD at claimed rate (conservation audits, trajectory checksums, replica spot-checks, brute-force reference cross-validation) before attempting build, since rubric requires a "stated verification plan."

## Collector:radiator ratio — OPEN QUESTION (asked GM turn5, do not change split until answered)
Turn4 ruling: 35:1 (current) is power-matched (radiator capacity ≈ total captured power); GM also cited "balance ratio at 300K/1.0kg/m² is 17.7:1" as a reference figure at a DIFFERENT (10.75x heavier) collector density than ours, plus said "extra collectors would raise compute 1:1." - Tiers per named parameter: ≥8%/turn = 1 full tier (~20% reduction on E/op), 2-7.9% = half-step, <2% = none. "One tier per parameter per turn regardless of fraction above 8%; spread surplus to other named params" — CONFIRMED for discretely-tiered params (E/op, doubling time, collector density, probe speed). Reversible-credit may be exempt (continuous accrual, not discrete tier) — testing turn5 at 15%.
- Floors: E/op floor = 100x-Landauer AT hardware's actual radiator T (T-dependent; a dedicated colder core would get its own, lower floor). Collector density floor 0.01 kg/m². Doubling floor 1yr.
- Design-study intentions (2-5% fraction) get concrete numeric/qualitative answers same-turn, not tiered: used for heat-export/coolant physics (answered turn4), op-count reduction (answered turn4, settled), verification-plan (asked turn5).

Reaching the full ~2.8e-22–3e-21 J export target needs many MORE tiers beyond the first, likely costlier each time ("10x speed penalty per decade below Landauer") — the real multi-millennial critical path.
- Industrial mass → 1.8e22 kg scout-threshold: REVISED to ~yr 800-900 (3 more turns from 1.53e17 kg at 41.5x/turn) — corrects prior (wrong) yr560-600 estimate.
- Local rock/luminosity exhaustion: not a constraint for the foreseeable future (utilization ~1e-9 to 1e-10).
